explanation: Reference executed successfully offline in ~4.8 s (exit 0, peak RSS ~0.54 GiB, far within the 600 s / 8 GiB limits), producing /work/outputs/ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv (2,484,403 bytes, controller sha256 8ba2ca5c...47d) with all three staged inputs verified byte-identical after the run. Observed evidence of fidelity to the notebook: the printed diagnostic "fraction of peaks without motifs 0.14" matches the notebook's stored output; the final df_peaks_maxmotif_clean.iloc[7:15] display reproduces the notebook's stored last-cell output row-for-row (e.g. chr9 124777413-124777783 fc 5.06479 with motif chr9 124777400-124777419 pval 450.0 strand '+', and chr1 67701045-67701415 with no motif), and the exported CSV equals the CSV from an independent exploratory run bit-for-bit. The endpoint table has the plan-assumed exact column set/order chrom,start,end,fc,chrom_2,start_2,end_2,pval_2,strand_2 with 40,557 rows; the 5,765 motif-less peaks export as empty CSV fields, confirming both plan assumptions. Input integrity: the two ENCODE files match their provider-published md5s (9dabac96..., 393688b4...) and byte sizes; the JASPAR track matches its published size (7,698,065 bytes) and a fixed md5 (0ebb5826...) recorded from this exact URL during setup, since that server publishes no checksum. Environment: bioframe 0.8.0 (current release; latest git revision of the notebook predates it), numpy 2.5.4, matplotlib 3.11.2 rendering headlessly via Agg (all plotting calls retained), and pandas pinned to 2.3.3 — pinned deliberately because pandas 3.0.6 was observed experimentally to silently discard the notebook's chained 'df[col].replace(-1, np.nan, inplace=True)' (leaking -1 into pval_2 and shifting every NaN downstream), while 2.3.3 only emits the same harmless FutureWarning the notebook always produced. The analysis.py diff vs original.py is limited to exactly three bioframe.read_table input-path string constants; all algorithms, parameters, seeds, comments, plots and branches are unchanged. One caveat: the controller's semantic-fidelity flag was not set, so this is a successful execution with matching notebook-stored outputs, not an independently certified equivalence.
source_adaptations: Three bioframe.read_table input-path constants changed from remote URLs to offline staged copies: the ENCODE peaks URL to '/inputs/ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz', the ENCODE blacklist URL to '/inputs/ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz', and 'jaspar_url + jaspar_motif_file' to '"/inputs/" + jaspar_motif_file' (jaspar_url and jaspar_motif_file definitions retained unchanged). The staged files are downloaded from those exact original URLs during setup and verified against provider md5s/sizes, so the bytes read by the analysis are unchanged; 'skiprows=1' and all schemas are untouched.

pandas pinned to 2.3.3 (with numpy>=2,<3 and matplotlib>=3.8 chosen for bioframe 0.8.0 compatibility on CPython 3.13.13). This is an environment choice, not a code change: pandas 3.x (Copy-on-Write) was observed to silently no-op the notebook's chained-assignment 'df_peaks_maxmotif["pval_2"].replace(-1, np.nan, inplace=True)', which would corrupt the exported pval_2 values; 2.3.3 reproduces the notebook-era behavior and only emits the pre-existing FutureWarning.
Matplotlib renders headlessly via the Agg backend (exported environment variable MPLBACKEND=Agg); the no-display base image has no other usable backend and no plotting call was removed or altered.
unresolved_assumptions: The JASPAR MA0139.1 hg38 2022 track is served without a provider checksum; integrity is asserted from its published size (7,698,065 bytes) plus the md5 of the exact bytes downloaded during this setup. If the upstream track were ever regenerated at the same size, the staged md5/size check would not distinguish the update from the bytes read by the original notebook.

bioframe 0.8.0 (PyPI current release) is used rather than the exact bioframe version in the notebook's CI at commit 95007ed; observed overlap/subtract/closest behavior reproduces the notebook's stored outputs, but a different bioframe minor version could in principle differ.

The tutorial's upstream URLs are assumed to remain the canonical distribution points for these three files; the staging recipe downloads from them and fails loudly (size/md5 mismatch) rather than substituting any mirror.

The recorded run is the controller's controller-executed reference (1 of 2 allowances used); the final controller report shows semantic_fidelity_validated false, so notebook-output agreement reported here (diag 0.14, matching iloc[7:15] rows, 40,557-row table, byte-identical duplicated run) is observed evidence from setup-stage verification rather than an independent fidelity certification.
